interactions.title: Kazuro’s knowledge, school and aid
lines: DM: There is a small raft docked at the dock, and sitting half submerged in the water is a stoneborn near the dock, skin bluish, like bluish gray limestone, wearing blue robes that seem not to be wet from the water, sitting still like a statue, the water up to his chest.
DM: And as you enter, sees your boat coming in the cave, he stands up, looks at you for a moment, and then grumbles in Common, "Who are you to disturb my meditation?"
DM: Begins to walk, and as he walks, you— he— he seems to be walking almost up underwater steps that lead up to the dock, and he comes and stands on the dock as you approach to tie up your ship.
Kenzo: What language is he speaking?
DM: He is annoyed and sort of a a bit grumpy to be interrupted.
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))

Delwath: So Delwath will apologize for the intrusion and explain that we come only due to great need, seeking the help of someone such as yourself, and explain sort of somewhat flatteringly, like, "We need your expertise," blah blah blah, that, you know, we heard of you in Castrella. We don't know this person's name, do we?
DM: You— the name— well, Kazuro is the name that you heard.

Delwath: And that we are part of a great story— mission— quest, where we are seeking information from the merfolk to the west, and we thought it was unwise to venture so far out to sea without a way of breathing the water, and we came seeking your advice on how we might achieve that, for we had heard tales that this is something you could do.
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))

DM: Looks around as you're speaking, like looking at all of you in turn, seeming particularly a— curious about the dwarves, about Seeker and Riswynn. And he kind of, you know, nods briefly, at least inviting you as far as to, like, you know, "Come up, get off your boat, come, sit down," saying, "Tell me more about this story. Everybody nowadays seeks to take shortcuts and not do the work, just come for favors. All I get are favor seekers. Why should your favor be so special?"
DM: And as he says this, as he says this, he's turning away and kind of walking up the stairs, like, "Follow me or not. I don't care."

Kenzo: Kenzo, as he starts to turn, says, "Favors may be only of the moment, but some stories can echo into the future for centuries. I'm capable of telling such stories, if that's of interest to you."
DM: He's— he says, as he's walking up the stairs, kind of to himself, not— not really paying attention if anybody is following or not.
DM: He says, "Indeed, there are many stories I've heard. The ocean has every story." Are you following him as— as...?
Delwath: Delwath is, at least, yeah. Yep.

Riswynn: Riswynn ventures to compliment, you know, "I, in the service of my gods, and attempts to be part of stories that make the world a better place. I've seen many wondrous things, and your home is quite remarkable."

DM: He, he kind of— so as you— he's sort of shaking his head a little bit as you go up these stairs. You see, as you get to the top of this set of stairs, there's a sort of a living area that's been set up. There's a— there's no, no walls or anything, but there's like a, a paper screen that he sort of pushes aside, and there's a series of windows that have been cleverly cut in the stone that allow sunlight to filter through and illuminate from this area. There's a bed, there's a simple hearth, a desk, a chest,

DM: And then there's a separate area that's sort of closed off, and he sort of motions. It's a fairly big room. He motions for you to sit on the floor and begin sort of bustling around making some— something, cooking water.
DM: And he's sort of talking as, as he, as he does this, saying, "You know, story is— quests— What is it that you even want from me? My help? Yes, that's what."
DM: "Everything I would give you I would take from the ocean to grant to you. Why should you have it? You've done nothing. Where are you from, anyway?"
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))
Kenzo: What? What? Yes, where are we from?
Riswynn: From the coastal mountains in the south.
Wellby: And Green— from the Green Sea.
Seeker: I'm in search of the merfolk. There's something that they— we think that they have, that we need.
DM: And why is it that something you deserve?
Wellby: Because it's not for us. It's for everybody. But...
DM: Starts pouring out some sort of tea. "Let it not be said I am inhospitable, but you have given me little reason to make sacrifices on your behalf."
Kenzo: Well, perhaps there's 2 potential motivations. As my friend Wellby says, our purpose in traveling into the oceans to try and meet the merfolk.

Kenzo: Our goal is to try to prevent the unleashing of a terrible evil that will undoubtedly impact you, impact these oceans in the months and years to come. We don't seek treasure, we don't seek glory. We seek to contain a dark and menacing evil that in 25 days—
Kenzo: 23 days. So there's great urgency in our, in our mission. So helping us would be of service actually to you, and also potentially to those that you care for, including the ocean.

Kenzo: So there's that. The other motivation, as I mentioned, and also my friend and fellow storyteller Wellby— I sense that— or we sense that— your presence here, perhaps your story and perhaps your works, perhaps they are meant for a larger— for it to be told, to be heard, and perhaps we might be able to help share your story.
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))
Riswynn: It would be noble work to learn from you, and not take shortcuts for our urgency not so great.
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))
Riswynn: I'm sure you have wonderful— you have great skills to teach, were there not peril close.

DM: Kenzo, you, when you're— when Kong— when Kenzo is talking about, like, fighting a great evil, you can sense something in his— you know, with your soul sight, something in his aura. He's reminiscing. He seems like he's sort of curious, but also like like there's— there's a tinge of sort of pain or trauma.
DM: Spreads through his aura when you're talking about fighting great evil. And says, as you're saying this, "Been in wars."
Kenzo: Yeah, I sense— I sense that you have experienced some— some such. You've confronted such evil yourself. You relate to our quest.
DM: "You know, the War of the Dark Rift. Umbral Covenant."
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))

DM: So yeah, he looks, as, you know, Seeker says, "Yeah, I know." "So I was surprised to see dwarves here. But as you say, you're from far away, and I don't know. there are strange songs on the oceans these days."
Seeker: Strange songs? Who sings them?
DM: "Well, whales, ocean itself, just a little...
DM: No matter the nobility of your quest do not know if I can give up my resources to those who are such novices I don't know. Wet."
Seeker: Between us, we have quite a depth of skill and lore, but under the— beneath the waves is a world less known to us. We are curious to learn.
DM: "I do wish I had somebody to teach. Grow old and weary."
Delwath: What is it that you would teach?
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))
DM: He looks— his sort of eyes light up for a minute when you ask that and he looks at Delwath, and he says—

DM: You know, he goes— he starts— he sort of talks animatedly for a while about everything that he's learned in a hundred years of listening to the ocean, and, and how it just takes— he seems particularly keen and eager that an elf asked him this and that nobody else would really understand. It takes decades to understand exactly what each each ripple in the water means, and the messages that each wave carries, and how to hear them, differences between— I'm— kinds of wind, and the kinds of waves, and the songs that drift from far to the west with their strange and uncanny beckoning noises, and the closer songs of the dolphins and the barking of the seals, and he sort of goes on and on about how he wishes he could— he had somebody he could share this with before, you know, "I will not be here forever. My— at 1 point, my body will become one with the stone, and slowly weather and turn to sand and drift endlessly on the currents, and when that happens, everything I've understood will be lost. The transformations that I can brew take what the ocean gives, and turn it into light," and he waves at his hands, "or gills, should you need them."
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))
Kenzo: Say, Kazuro, "As a human, my lifespan is short relative to yours or to the elf."((Lifespan clarification))
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))
Kenzo: And he says, "The individual lifespans of humans are, are short relative to those of you and the dwarves, but perhaps this may be of interest to you. I'm establishing a school of sorts."
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))

Kenzo: Kenzo, as, as he, as he speaks, you know, kind of, like, shows his— shows this, like, network of, like, glowing tattoos that he has glow, you know, blue like, like the ocean, kind of traveling up and down his arm and also up and down a staff.
Kenzo: And I says, "I'm a student of many of the Dunmari gods who have persisted for generations, for millennia."((Historical-duration clarification))
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))

Kenzo: "And I'm seeking my own legacy, my own path forward, and I'm establishing a monastery, a place where the teachings that I've learned can be passed on for generations to come, and in true earnest, I want to set one up here. I want to establish such a place where acolytes can learn, but also be connected deeply to to nature, to the environment that surrounds them. Learn to hear and see the way that you do, the way you've described the relationship that you have with the ocean. It's incredible."
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))

Kenzo: "This entire region speaks to me. I feel something very magnetic here, and I want to establish a school here. If you were so— if this would be of interest to you, it might, it may be a way for you to pass on your teachings."
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))

Delwath: All the, all these things to learn, the— Delwath will certainly say, you know, express some interest in all these things about the ocean, but also at some point sort of say, "My calling is not this," right? My calling— and I don't know, demonstrate some magic. "You know, my calling is to help the humans and learn from these gods— the heat, the— the human— learn from the human gods and carry their magic."
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))

Delwath: We travel widely, right? I'll mention, you know, we've— we've already collect— yeah, we, we, we have collected a number of companions, right, who, you know— I'll talk about the Frost Giant and a few other folks. You know, we encounter, it seems, odd people across our journeys quite regularly, and we would be honored to seek an apprentice for you should you wish it. And should Kenzo— you know, should you seek something more solitary then Kenzo's offer— should you be looking for something— yeah, I don't— I don't wanna undercut. That was not trying to undercut Kenzo's offer, right? Like, not...
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))
DM: So he's, he's sort of looking, sort of— looking pleased at, at, at both of you. And, and Kenzo, you, you get the sense that he's genuinely intrigued by your offer.
Kenzo: And I'm genuinely intrigued. Like, I really like— Kenzo likes this place. Like, he, he genuinely is like, live in this place.
DM: And he he looks back at, at Delwath as well. "That is— how do I say this?— did not expect such an offer."
DM: And he, and he looks over again at Kenzo, and he says, "I, I can see the ocean has made an impact on you."
DM: "You are carrying around a piece of ocean ki on your staff."
Kenzo: Oh, Tim! What's the start— what's the name of the— what's the name of my, my acolyte?

Kenzo: Oh, and sorry I'm sorry. What's this guy? Isn't the guy's name again? Kazuro. On— "It has, and if it would please you as it would please me, I have a student that I could— I could introduce you to, to begin this process as soon as you would like. We could learn from you."

DM: He sort of— he sort of smiles now. Like, the— this whole time has been sort of bustling around in the, in the— his hearth, and he's starting to put out some snacks as well, some like little sushi rolls and...
DM: Seaweed and, like, you know, rice and some raw fish. And he—
DM: "There is— there is no need to rush. I am— I am not— I am not dying tomorrow. I am touched by your generosity and your consideration. I would— whoever— whoever you find,"
DM: And he looks at both Kenzo and Delwath together, "Think the 2 of you would be a good judge of, who might be a student who would appreciate my teachings. Strengths balance each other."
Kenzo: Delwath likes to cook. I like to eat.
DM: "I would— I have long sought to build a small school, a small monastery here on this island."
DM: "No, you are— know that— know that you have pressing urgent business, and this not urgent. This can be the matter of years."
Kenzo: Kenzo stands and, like, just stares him, like, super, just deep, like, in the eyes. And it's like, "I pledge I will return and build the school with you."
DM: And he looks over, "And the elf will help find students?"
Kenzo: I don't know, but we'll see what the elf wants to do.
Delwath: Of course. You said you were unsettled by news from the west.
DM: "It has been a few years now since the discordant notes have reached me. I don't know what it might mean. But I suspect you are venturing into danger if you are seeking the merfolk."
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))

Delwath: The— we are seeking— something, I fear, has corrupted the kelp forests, something that has changed peace to slaughtering— command— you know, changed singing to commanding amongst the merfolk to the west.

DM: "Perhaps so. It is far from here, and only distant echoes of the songs of that ocean reach me. But what I have heard does suggest violence and discord. what more may be happening I do not know. Not left this island in some time, this..."
Delwath: Discord is upsetting to the ocean, we assume, and against the natural order. Is that right?
Delwath: So any guesses or wisdom you could share that might help us as we venture towards it would be worth— would be—
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))

DM: He— so, I mean, he's been— he's been fiddling with things this whole time, and you see that he's been— his hands are sort of always working, and he has this— he's pulled out this sort of very elaborate sort of set of, like— it's like a really massive, like, spice cabinet or something, and he's been fiddling around with little things and seems to be, you know, making something while he talks. Like, his hands are always kind of moving around while he talks, like cooking or making tea or or doing this.

DM: He sort of looks over, you know, again, he's clearly pleased by the, by the offer and everything, and the way the conversation's going. And he sort of reacts to your, to your message sort of almost in surprise. Like, "I, I thought it was clear I'm, I'm making things for you."
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))

Delwath: I know. No, no, no, no, I— I'm after information. So it's more like, we— I wanna tell them, "We, we know we are— we are well versed in the air and the mountains and the forests and the plains. We understand the city, we know, you know, the mountain peaks. We fought battles in, you know, the North and a vampire's castle. Those places we all understand. We don't really understand the ocean. What should we know? We don't have a year to learn from you, or a decade like we should."
DM: "Further west you go in the Encircling Sea, ocean has its own dreams, its own thoughts."
Delwath: We knew it was out there.
Kenzo: And it's the ocean and...
Delwath: How can we avoid offending it?
DM: "It is an alien thing. Have never traveled that far, but the merfolk speak to it. They dream with it. Listen to what they say. Follow their guide."
Seeker: Are the merfolk allies to you?
DM: "They are not allies to anybody but the ocean."
Delwath: There may be some conflict among the merfolk, we fear. We would seek your advice on navigating that. How do we know which ones still dream of the ocean?
DM: "I am sorry I cannot solve this riddle for you."
Delwath: Would you like to come with us?
Delwath: Didn't think so. But I thought I'd ask.
DM: Takes— as he's been working, he takes out 6 little packets that he's wrapped in seaweed.

DM: "But maybe this will help you." And he unwraps one, and you can see that there's, like, sort of 2 sort of gummy globules of, of some kind of, like, herbal concoction, like a jelly sort of thing. One is, like, a deep blue, the other is almost perfectly clear.
DM: He holds this up. "The deep blue will turn your lungs into gills. You will cease to be able to breathe air, but you'll be able to breathe water."
Seeker: How long does that last?

DM: "Until you take the pale, clear white, which will turn your gills back into lungs. Be warned, this is magic, and it can be dispelled, but otherwise will not end until you consume the antidote. we have 6 doses, enough for you, plus one extra that I can share. I can make more, but it will take time. I don't know if you have time to spare."
Seeker: Not a lot. We would be grateful to have these. I don't...
Riswynn: Last thing that I could have hoped.
Delwath: It would— we are quite grateful, and perhaps, if you would be willing, you would make more after we leave, in case we need it.
DM: "I will replenish my stocks, yes."
((Rolls, rules, historical digression and repeated or unrelated table discussion))
DM: He hands these 6 packets over.
DM: "Stay as long as you wish, but I understand if urgency drives you, when I listen to you again, when you return to fulfill your promises."

Kenzo: Kenzo, you know, gives them a— you know, a long, a long glance, and then says, "When I return, it would be an honor to hear your story. I, as part of my tradition, capture stories in materials, wood carvings. It'd be an honor to hear your story and to, and to capture it."

DM: "Story is a long one, and perhaps for when we have more time. Indeed, after the war, I travel widely before settling here. There are some strange things in the far north of this world where there is ice even in summer that floats on the oceans."
Kenzo: Look forward to hearing those tales.
